body: @Jora28 I'm unable to reproduce the issue with the current information. Can you please share the exact steps to reproduce the issue. this looks to be similar if not a duplicate of an existing issue #8261

I hit this too and managed to reduce it to a **one-dependency reproduction**. Posting the details since the issue is currently marked as hard to reproduce.

## Minimal reproduction

```json
{
  "name": "repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "@vitejs/devtools": "*"
  }
}
```

```
npm install --package-lock-only
```

```
npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')
```

Same crash site as the original report (`#loadPeerSet`, `build-ideal-tree.js:1289`). No lock file and no `node_modules` needed — it fails during ideal-tree construction.

## The trigger is the *range*, not the resolved version

This is the part I found most interesting. All three resolve to the same version (`0.4.2`), but only the wildcard crashes:

| `@vitejs/devtools` range | npm 10.9.8 |
| --- | --- |
| `"*"` | **`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`** |
| `"^0.4.2"` | OK |
| `"0.4.2"` | OK |

Verified deterministic — repeated in fresh directories with a clean cache state, consistently reproducible.

## Version matrix

| Manifest | npm 10.9.8 (arborist 8.0.5) | npm 11.18.0 (arborist 9.9.0) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"@vitejs/devtools": "*"}` | `reading 'edgesOut'` (build-ideal-tree.js:1289) | `reading 'children'` (place-dep.js:299) |
| `{"nuxt": "3.21.1"}` | `reading 'edgesOut'` | — |
| `{"nuxt": "4.5.0"}` | `reading 'edgesOut'` | OK |
| `{"@nuxt/vite-builder": "4.5.0"}` | `reading 'edgesOut'` | OK |
| `{"vite": "*"}` | OK | OK |

Two notes on npm 11: it still crashes on the isolated `@vitejs/devtools` case, just with a different null dereference. But on a larger real-world manifest that pulls `@vitejs/devtools` in transitively it resolved fine (1070 packages), presumably because the surrounding constraints keep the graph from reaching the bad state. So npm 11 is not a general fix here.

## Why it's null

`build-ideal-tree.js:1289` in arborist 8.0.5 is:

```js
const parentEdge = node.parent.edgesOut.get(edge.name)
```

so `node.parent` is `null`. The stack shows `#loadPeerSet` recursing into itself (line 1297 → 1289), i.e. the node gets detached from its parent partway through recursive peer-set resolution and is then dereferenced unguarded. The npm 11 failure is the same shape one layer over — `virtualRoot.children` at `place-dep.js:299` with a null `virtualRoot`.

The likely reason `@vitejs/devtools` provokes it is its peer block — four **optional** peers that are self-referential siblings at the same version, plus a wildcard:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "vite": "*",
  "@vitejs/devtools-rolldown": "^0.4.2",
  "@vitejs/devtools-vite": "^0.4.2",
  "@vitejs/devtools-vitest": "^0.4.2",
  "@vitejs/devtools-oxc": "^0.4.2"
},
"peerDependenciesMeta": {
  "@vitejs/devtools-oxc":      { "optional": true },
  "@vitejs/devtools-rolldown": { "optional": true },
  "@vitejs/devtools-vite":     { "optional": true },
  "@vitejs/devtools-vitest":   { "optional": true }
}
```

Each of those sub-packages installs cleanly on its own; only the parent that declares the optional-sibling peer set crashes.

## Why Nuxt users are the ones reporting this

`nuxt` → `@nuxt/vite-builder` → `@vitejs/devtools`. Since npm auto-installs peers, anything that peer-depends on `@nuxt/schema` or `nuxt` drags the whole builder toolchain in. `{"nuxt": "3.21.1"}` — the version in the original report — reproduces the exact `edgesOut` error as a single dependency on npm 10.

I ran into it in a different context: a Nuxt/Nitro server bundle that externalises a package peer-depending on `@nuxt/schema`, deployed to Firebase Cloud Functions. The Node 22 buildpack ships npm 10, so the deploy build died with this error while a local npm 11 install of the same manifest succeeded.

## Workaround

Skipping peer auto-install avoids it, since none of that tooling is needed at runtime:

```
# .npmrc
legacy-peer-deps=true
```

Confirmed: `{"@vitejs/devtools": "*"}` goes from crash to OK on npm 10.9.8 with that set. Pinning the offending package to an exact or caret range instead of `*` also works, where you control the range.

## Environment

```
npm:  10.9.8 (arborist 8.0.5) — crashes
npm:  11.18.0 (arborist 9.9.0) — crashes differently on the isolated case
Node: v24.15.0
OS:   Windows 11 (26200); also reproduces on the Linux Node 22 GCP buildpack
```

`@vitejs/devtools` resolved to `0.4.2` at time of testing — noting it since the `*` range is what makes this reproduce, so future registry state may shift which version you land on.

@Jora28 Actually, I also faced this issue. This issue is resolved by updating the nodejs and npm version to their latest versions.
Upgraded Node.js (v22.21.1 → v24.x) and npm (v10.9.4 → v11.x), resolving the npm install failure.

I hit this through a generated application, then reduced that real-world graph to a second one-dependency reproduction that may help pin the affected peer-set shape.

## Minimal reproduction

```json
{
  "name": "vitest-edgesout-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "vitest": "4.1.4"
  }
}
```

From a fresh directory with no lock file or `node_modules`:

```sh
npx --yes npm@10.9.9 install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts
```

Result:

```text
npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')
```

The verbose stack is the same recursive `#loadPeerSet` path reported above:

```text
at #loadPeerSet (.../@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1289:38)
at async #loadPeerSet (.../build-ideal-tree.js:1297:11)
at async #loadPeerSet (.../build-ideal-tree.js:1297:11)
at async #loadPeerSet (.../build-ideal-tree.js:1297:11)
```

I repeated it with a new, isolated npm cache and `--prefer-online`; it failed identically.

## Version boundary

Using otherwise identical one-dependency manifests:

| Manifest | npm 10.9.9 |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest@4.1.4` | crashes reading `edgesOut` |
| `vitest@4.1.9` | crashes reading `edgesOut` |
| `vitest@4.1.10` | succeeds |
| `vitest@^4.1.10` | succeeds |

For `vitest@4.1.4`:

| npm | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 10.9.9 | crashes reading `edgesOut` |
| 11.19.0 | succeeds |
| 12.0.2 | succeeds |

`--legacy-peer-deps` also makes the npm 10.9.9 install succeed.

The npm 10 verbose fetch sequence reaches `@vitejs/devtools` and its optional sibling peers immediately before the recursive `#loadPeerSet` failure, so this appears consistent with the optional-peer analysis in the reproduction above. The original application dependency graph is not required to trigger it.

Environment:

```text
Node: v24.18.0
OS: macOS / Darwin 25.5.0, arm64
npm: 10.9.9, 11.19.0, 12.0.2
```

**Deterministic reproduction** (hit us in CI twice in 2 months; this instance reproduces locally every time):

```json
{ "devDependencies": { "vitest": "4.1.10", "jsdom": "29.1.1", "vite": "7.1.1" } }
```

`npm install --force` (no lockfile) -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` at `#loadPeerSet` (`build-ideal-tree.js:1297`), npm 10.9.2 / node 22.13.1.

**Trigger**: `vitest@4.1.11` was published ~90 seconds before our install ran. vitest declares its family (`@vitest/browser-playwright`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, ...) as *optional peers pinned to its own version*; with the root pinned to `4.1.10` and the registry's latest at `4.1.11`, evaluating that optional peer set - for packages we never install - crashes the resolver instead of raising a readable `ERESOLVE`. Aligning the root pin to `4.1.11` makes the install pass, which is how we isolated the peer-set version skew as the trigger.

Notable: the crash comes from the *declaration* of an optional peer alone - `@vitest/browser-playwright` is never installed in this tree (`npm ls` -> empty).

Full `--verbose` stack and debug log available on request.

Confirming this on npm 10.9.2 / Node v23.11.0 (macOS, Darwin 25.6.0), same crash site (`#loadPeerSet`, `build-ideal-tree.js`), triggered by bumping `vitest` from `3.2.6` to `^4.1.11` in an existing project (not a fresh minimal repro) — so this also hits normal upgrade workflows, not just fresh installs of a pinned range.

Two additional data points that might help:

1. **`npm install --legacy-peer-deps` "succeeds" but produces a broken lockfile.** It avoids the crash, but the resulting `package-lock.json` then fails `npm ci` on the same npm version with `Missing: undici-types@5.26.5 from lock file`. So this flag isn't a safe workaround — it silently produces a lockfile that isn't valid for reproducible installs.
2. **`npx --yes npm@11 install` (v11.18.0) resolves cleanly** with no flags needed, and the lockfile it produces is then consumable by the original npm 10.9.2 via both `npm install` and `npm ci` without any crash — the bug only seems to hit *ideal-tree construction from scratch*, not consumption of an already-correctly-resolved lockfile.

For anyone hitting this on an existing project: regenerating the lockfile once via `npx --yes npm@11 install` (no need to change your global/CI npm version) seems to be a clean fix.

Reproduction without a wildcard range, in case it helps get this off "Cannot Reproduce". Fails on npm ≤ 11.5.0, passes on 11.6.0.

Empty directory, no lock file, no `node_modules`:

```json
{ "name": "m", "version": "1.0.0", "private": true }
```

```console
$ npm i -D vitest@4.1.11
npm error Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')
```

`npx --yes vitest@4.1.11` and `npm exec --package=vitest@4.1.11 -- vitest` hit the same crash, and so does `npm i` on its own — so this is not `npx`-specific. It is specific to the manifest, though: a dependency-free package such as `cowsay@1.6.0` installs fine.

## Version boundary

| npm | result |
| --- | --- |
| 10.8.2 | FAIL |
| 10.9.0 | FAIL |
| 10.9.4 | FAIL |
| 11.0.0 | FAIL |
| 11.5.0 | FAIL |
| 11.6.0 | OK |
| 11.7.0 | OK |
| 11.8.0 | OK |
| 11.9.0 | OK |
| 11.19.1 | OK |

Reproduced on Node 26.10.0 / Linux, each version installed with `npm i -g npm@<version>`, `node_modules` and `package-lock.json` removed before every run, result taken from the exit code.

## Two things that differ from the `@vitejs/devtools: "*"` case above

Worth checking whether these are one bug or two:

1. **Different fix boundary.** The table in the previous comment has `{"@vitejs/devtools": "*"}` still failing on npm 11.18.0, while this manifest has been fine since 11.6.0. If 11.6.0 only fixed one of the two code paths, the other is still open.
2. **Deeper recursion in the stack.** Mine is `#loadPeerSet` sync frame plus **three** recursive async frames, the previous one has a single async frame:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')
    at #loadPeerSet (@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1286:38)
    at async #loadPeerSet (@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1294:11)
    at async #loadPeerSet (@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1294:11)
    at async #loadPeerSet (@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:1294:11)
    at async #buildDepStep (@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:901:11)
    at async Arborist.buildIdealTree (@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js:181:7)
    at async Arborist.reify (@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/reify.js:131:5)
    at async Install.exec (npm/lib/commands/install.js:150:5)
```

A different recursion depth suggests a different cycle in the peer graph, not the same one reached by a different manifest.

I hit this in a StackBlitz project, where npm 10.8.2 ships in the container and `npx --yes <pkg>@<version>` is the normal way to run a second version of a tool, so it blocks running a project against two versions of one dependency. Switching the container to pnpm worked around it.

The crash is in arborist's `#loadPeerSet` (`workspaces/arborist/lib/arborist/build-ideal-tree.js`), and it's the same defect as #8261 — already fixed by #8448.

While iterating `peerEdges`, the recursive `#nodeFromEdge` call can resolve a compatible peer that **replaces the current node and detaches it from the tree**. The node loses its parent, and the very next statement — `node.parent.edgesOut.get(edge.name)` — throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`.

#8448 added a guard at the top of that loop:

```js
for (const edge of peerEdges) {
  // node.parent gets mutated during loop execution due to recursive #nodeFromEdge calls.
  // When a compatible peer is found (e.g. a@1.1.0 replaces a@1.2.0), the original node loses its parent.
  // if node is detached/removed from the tree, or has no parent, so no need to check remaining edgesOut for that node.
  if (!node.parent) {
    break
  }
```

### Version boundary

That guard first shipped in arborist **9.1.4** — i.e. **npm 11.6.0**. Confirmed by fetching `build-ideal-tree.js` from each release tag and grepping for it:

| npm | arborist | guard present | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11.5.0 | 9.1.3 | no | crash |
| 11.6.0 | 9.1.4 | yes | ok |
| 11.19.1 | — | yes | ok |

This lines up exactly with @Addin's bisect.

So this is a fixed issue rather than `Cannot Reproduce`. The vitest trigger is real — a package pinning a whole family of optional peers to its own version while the root sits one patch behind — but from 11.6.0 on, arborist lets the compatible peer back off instead of crashing.

`--legacy-peer-deps` only appears to "work" because it skips this code path entirely, which is also why it leaves an incomplete lockfile.

We hit the same `edgesOut` crash and tested which npm versions are affected. Repro and results:

**Repro** (empty directory, no lockfile, Node 22.12.0):

```
echo '{"name":"x","private":true}' > package.json
npm install vitest@4.1.11
```

**Results**

| npm | Result |
|---|---|
| 10.9.0 (bundled with Node 22.12) | fails: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` |
| 10.9.9 (newest npm 10.x) | fails, same error |
| 11.5.2 | fails, same error |
| 11.6.0 | installs |
| 11.21.1 | installs |

The same npm 10.9.9 also fails on Node 22.23.4, so a newer Node 22 patch doesn't avoid it. `vitest@4.0.18` installs on npm 10.9.x.

**Takeaway for us:** the crash needs npm 11.6.0 or later. Node 22 still bundles npm 10.9.x, so CI on Node 22 has to upgrade npm first. If you want a different repro, we can provide one.
